sections.h2: Fast-sale options for a Houston owner
sections.html:
Houston owners choose among a broker listing, a private sale and a cash offer. This is a market unto itself, with 2,397,315 people at the 2025 estimate, and prices change a great deal from one street to the next.

Owners occupy only 42.1% of Houston homes, so landlords, investors and first-time buyers all bid for houses. Cash tends to suit a house with postponed upkeep, storm damage, a tenant or a cloudy title. A listing works best for a house that shows well.

  • Locate the deed and any survey, and learn whether deed restrictions cover your street.
  • Confirm the appraisal district and taxing units for the address.
  • Collect two written offers, each naming a closing date.

sections.h2: No zoning, but deed restrictions and plats
sections.html:
Houston has no citywide zoning. Voters rejected it, and subdivision deed restrictions steer most construction. Such private restrictions can limit what gets built and how a lot is used. Read yours and give a copy to the buyer.

The city's planning department requires a plat, a surveyed map of the lot, before building permits. Single-family classification can include a duplex or a garage apartment under 900 square feet unless the deed restrictions forbid it. Houston also reviews plats in an area about five miles beyond its limits, where its permit and inspection rules do not apply.

Plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office after approval. The city's planning site has a map viewer and a Plat Tracker for searching by address.

For 2020 to 2024 the midpoint home value is $277,800, and owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,240 a month. That midpoint covers the whole city, so use it only as background and trust written offers for your own house.

sections.h2: Harris Central Appraisal District and exemptions
sections.html:
Most Houston property is valued for tax by the Harris Central Appraisal District. Owners can file protests, renditions and homestead exemptions on its site, which also has an Exemption Wizard. A deed protection feature lets you register your home with the Harris County Clerk as a guard against deed fraud.

The valuation date is January 1. Homestead notices start near April 1. Your protest is due by May 15, or 30 days after the notice if that is later. A disappointing board ruling can be carried to district court or binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value passes $1,000,000. Owners who appeal generally pay the undisputed portion on time.

  • With the exemption active, a homestead's appraised value cannot climb more than 10% in a year.
  • An heir whose name is not on the recorded deed needs an ownership affidavit, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.
  • Someone who closes after January 1 may still apply for the remainder of the year if the seller never did.

Your tax bill shows which district and taxing units cover the parcel.

Buyers and lenders will want answers. Paving and fast runoff have long fed flooding here, and severe floods in 1929 and 1935 led to the Harris County Flood Control District and later the Addicks and Barker reservoirs.

The city says flood mitigation, drainage, water and sewer are outside the Planning Commission's plat review, so a plat does not settle a house's flood risk. Request flood records for your address from the city and the county, and put repair records and insurance claims in a folder for buyers.

Heat, humidity and heavy rain are hard on roofs, siding and air conditioning. Cash buyers accept storm damage as is, and a clear paper trail helps both sides settle on a price.

Buyers often search by neighborhood. Houston Heights and Pasadena grew as developer-built suburbs in 1892, Bellaire in 1911, West University Place in 1919 and River Oaks in the mid-1920s, and those names still anchor listing descriptions. Several of them are separate municipalities, so check whether your address sits inside Houston or in another city, because that decides who issues permits and which rules apply.

Say how long it takes to drive to downtown, the Texas Medical Center or the ship channel, since the average commute is 27.2 minutes and buyers weigh it. Confirm your school district on the tax bill or with the district before you print it in a listing.

Build a single folder before you list or accept anything. Include the deed, any survey, the deed restrictions for your subdivision, your latest tax statement and payoff letters for each loan. Add flood records, repair receipts and insurance claims for the house.

In a market this large buyers compare many houses, and a seller who can answer with documents closes faster. Ask each bidder to state price, closing date, who pays closing charges and what happens if the deal falls through, then compare what you would net after payoffs.

Unless the lease says otherwise, the written notice to vacate is three days, and an eviction suit begins in justice court with a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. A tenant has five days from judgment to appeal to county court, and the writ of possession waits six days after final judgment.

Put the tenant's presence in writing for every buyer and attach the lease. Investors may keep the tenant, but a buyer moving in needs the house empty at closing.

Texas repealed its inheritance tax effective September 1, 2015. Probate should be opened within four years of a death, and the small estate affidavit is limited to estates of up to $75,000 apart from the homestead.

Deeds are recorded by county clerks. Before meeting buyers, heirs should collect the death certificate, any will and a recent tax statement, because the title company will ask who has legal power to sign.

Unpaid taxes leave the January 1 lien on the house, and penalty plus interest start on February 1. If nothing is paid, a taxing unit may sue and have the property auctioned.

A sale ahead of that avoids it. At closing the title company takes the balance from your proceeds, so get a payoff figure early and judge each offer by what is left once it is paid.

The title company searches the record, asks for payoff letters and checks how your parcel stands on taxes. It drafts the deed and a settlement statement, and you should read both before closing day.

Signing takes place in front of a notary. Once the deed is recorded, payoffs and charges come out and the rest is yours. With cash there is no lender approval or appraisal, which helps the date hold. Disclose repairs, storm damage or a tenant to the buyer up front, and time your move so the house is empty when the keys change hands. File your own copies of every signed page and the settlement statement with your yearly tax papers.

faqs.a: Houston covers 640.44 square miles of land and counts 2,397,315 residents at the 2025 estimate. Verify the county and appraisal district for your own address before you rely on any tax figure.
Not citywide. Voters turned it down, but private deed restrictions and the city's plat and permit rules still apply, so read your restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Houston property value?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days of receiving your notice if that is later. The Harris Central Appraisal District site accepts online filing.

faqs.q: Where do I find the plat for my lot?
faqs.a: After approval, plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office. The city's planning site offers a map viewer and a Plat Tracker that search by address.
That is a citywide midpoint from the 2020 to 2024 survey. Your own house needs written offers or an appraisal.
